finding: The pain is real and urgent, but the generic assessment/Graph-sync offer is already being commercialized by established Dynamics/CRM integration vendors. Wealth Engine should not build another generic connector before proving a narrower channel or price advantage.

facts: Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement on-premises to Exchange Online uses EWS.
No new tenants have been connected to this feature since 2025-10-01 and it receives no new updates.
2026-10-01 is Microsoft's recommended deadline to migrate or allow-list EWS temporarily.
2027-04-01 is the end of support for Dynamics CRM Customer Engagement v9.0 on-premises with Exchange Online.

Microsoft's supported strategic paths are Dynamics 365 online or supported Exchange Server on-premises; keeping CRM on-premises with Exchange Online therefore requires a third-party/custom continuity path.

commercial_competitors.name: Riva
commercial_competitors.evidence: Riva explicitly markets a Graph-based sync layer as a way to keep Dynamics CRM on-premises with Exchange Online after EWS retirement; its 2026 releases already use its Modern Microsoft Exchange Connector (Graph).
commercial_competitors.implication: Strong validation of willingness-to-pay and technical feasibility, but weakens a generic connector thesis.

commercial_competitors.name: Synoptek
commercial_competitors.evidence: Offers a named Dynamics CRM Exposure Assessment specifically for the EWS retirement risk.
commercial_competitors.implication: The low-friction assessment wedge is already validated commercially, but is not differentiated by itself.

commercial_competitors.name: enCloud9
commercial_competitors.evidence: Actively markets migration services around the EWS retirement and Dynamics on-premises risk.
commercial_competitors.implication: Partners are already educating their installed bases; they can be competitors or channels.

commercial_competitors.name: Stoneridge Software
commercial_competitors.evidence: Published a dedicated 2026 warning for CRM on-premises 9.x customers about EWS retirement.
commercial_competitors.implication: Confirms an active partner channel with customer exposure, but also means simple advisory content is commoditized.

fresh_demand_signal.signal: An administrator reports an active Dynamics 365 on-premises deployment failing to connect after Exchange mailboxes were moved to Exchange Online, despite S2S certificate and tenant configuration, and says a Microsoft support ticket had not resolved it.
fresh_demand_signal.interpretation: There is not only future deadline risk; live hybrid/on-prem transition failures already create support demand.

revised_offer_strategy.do_not_build_yet: generic Graph sync replacement for Dynamics CRM on-premises
revised_offer_strategy.reason: Riva already supplies a mature Graph-based synchronization layer and Microsoft migration partners can sell broader cloud migrations.
revised_offer_strategy.best_near_term_wedge: EWS Dependency Triage for Microsoft partners/MSPs
revised_offer_strategy.buyer: small and mid-sized Microsoft/Dynamics partners that have legacy CRM on-premises customers but do not maintain their own Graph synchronization product
delivery: identify affected CRM version and Exchange topology
verify EWS usage and mailbox workflows
produce a continuity decision: temporary allow-list, Riva/third-party layer, Exchange on-premises, custom bridge, or Dynamics online migration
optionally white-label the assessment for the partner
revised_offer_strategy.why_better: It monetizes urgency without taking on the engineering/support burden of competing with Riva. The partner already owns the customer relationship, reducing acquisition cost.

gate.status: commercial pain validated; distribution wedge unvalidated
gate.next_test: Identify 20 small/mid-sized Dynamics partners/MSPs with evidence of on-premises CRM work. Exclude firms already selling their own EWS/Graph continuity product. Rank by reachable decision-maker, legacy CRM specialization and absence of a published EWS solution.
gate.pass: At least 8 plausible channel partners remain after exclusions and at least 3 show recent Dynamics CRM on-premises work or explicit legacy support.
gate.fail: The reachable partner set is dominated by firms already selling migration/continuity solutions, making channel acquisition expensive or adversarial.

decision: No new website or Railway deployment yet. Distribution evidence is the next scarce information.
